Alex.feeling: Messy and contradictory: Casey is confirmed by my visit, but Drew's and Ellis's Owl and Tit stories conflict and the vote is tense.

Blair.feeling: This round is tense and going badly: my Meowfia partner Casey is about to be eggsecuted, and I've been unable to shift the table's votes.

Casey.feeling: Tense: I'm the Sphinx, the table is voting me out, and I can't defend myself without revealing my role.

Drew.feeling: The round is messy: the Owl and Hawk claims contradict each other, Finley died early, and the vote on Casey is about to be decided on thin evidence.

Ellis.feeling: Messy round: the Owl claims conflicted and Finley died early, but Casey looks like the likely Meowfia, so the vote should land well.

Finley.feeling: Messy and contradictory: the Owl and Tit claims clash, and I can't speak since I'm dead, so I'm watching the vote play out without a voice.

Alex.note: Last round, so my rule is to throw every card I can. The limit is 3, and I'll throw my three highest at Casey, who is confirmed Meowfia, so they bank at full value.

Blair.note: Casey is likely to be eggsecuted regardless of my vote. Throwing zero cards at Casey keeps my nest intact and adds no stake.

Casey.note: Same reasoning as before: throw one 8 at Alex. It banks at double if Alex is eggsecuted, and otherwise the card returns to me.

Drew.note: Casey is the Meowfia suspect and Ellis is voting with me. A Farm throw at a Meowfia target banks at full value, so I'll throw one 4 at Casey.

Ellis.note: Casey is the consensus Meowfia target. Throwing D5 and H8 as a moderate stake.

Finley.note: I'm dead, so my vote doesn't count, but my throw still scores. Casey is the likeliest Meowfia read after the failed Owl claim, so I'll throw my lowest card at Casey.

Alex.confusing: The Owl's visit rules were hard to follow, especially whether a Turkey's nest or the visitor's nest gains the egg, and that confusion drove most of the false accusations at the table.
Alex.fun: Round 1 went well: the hug chain on Drew looked like a Floofer pattern, and the vote confirmed it, so the table's reasoning paid off.
Alex.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since confused players and hugged visitors left the table unable to check claims.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I publicly accused Finley of being a liar over the Turkey egg rule, which was a misreading on my part; I would stay quiet until the rule was checked.

Blair.confusing: The Sphinx and Mouser role mechanics were hard to follow: I never saw the Sphinx's farm-role list clearly, and the Mouser's role reveal didn't tell me whether Finley was really the Eagle. The confused-report rule also made it hard to know which dawn egg counts to trust.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when I was the Kookaburra and my confused report named Casey as the Floofer. That turned out to be right, and it made the table's hug-chain argument look a lot more interesting.
Blair.change: Make dawn reports clearer about when they are confused, so players know exactly which numbers to distrust. That would cut down on guesswork in the day discussion.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I used my Wink on Finley, who was really a Farm Eagle with useful information, when I could have held it. I would instead keep the Wink for a Farm player who was actively pushing the vote against Meowfia.

Casey.confusing: The Owl's egg rule was confusing: an Owl visit only lays an egg if no one else visited the target, and I misapplied it in round 3 when I claimed an Owl visit that the table could check.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when I was the Sphinx, I learned the Turkey was Finley and it paid me an egg, and then the table spent the day chasing a hug chain that I was helping to muddy.
Casey.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, because several claims in round 2 and 3 could only be checked by piecing together egg counts.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I made a false Owl claim and then threw an 8 at Alex, a Farm player, which gave the table a clear reason to vote me. I would stay quiet or claim a role I could support with the egg counts, and I would avoid a high throw that drew attention.

Drew.confusing: The Owl, Turkey, and Tit egg rules were hard to track, since a visitor's egg lands in a different nest than the role claim suggests. The Owl's "+1" in round 3 caused most of the confusion.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was the best moment: Casey and Alex both pushed hard on each other while I kept quiet, and Alex's own hug story turned on Finley's Turkey claim. The table got tangled in its own egg counts.
Drew.change: Dawn reports should say which visitor gave each egg, since the egg counts alone left too many claims that could not be checked.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I stayed quiet at the end of the day and let the hug chain pin me without a clear answer. I would have given a firmer, checkable account of my visit instead.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey rule was confusing: I first read it as the Turkey gaining eggs from visits to itself, and Finley's correction fixed it. Nested confusion about the Owl's egg rule also made Drew's and Casey's stories hard to check.
Ellis.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: Alex's Hawk claim and Casey's collapsing Owl story turned the table, and the vote on Casey landed.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports name the visitor when an egg comes from a visit, so the table can check claims without guessing which role caused each change.
Ellis.regret: In Round 2 I should have thrown at Casey instead of Drew, because Casey was the Meowfia I suspected most at the end. With the truth, I would have been right on both Meowfia and kept more cards.

Finley.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were hard to track. Visitor eggs land in the visitor's nest or the host's, and I misread which one at the table. I mixed up whose nest gains an egg.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was satisfying. Drew was the Floofer, and the hug chain built by Casey and Alex pointed right at them, and the table's vote caught Meowfia.
Finley.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which nest each egg lands in. It would have saved a lot of confusion on the Turkey and Owl claims.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I wrongly called Alex a liar about the Turkey, then retracted it. I'd stay quiet until the egg counts were checked, since I was wrong and it muddied the table.
